judge: Claude Code subagent, Claude Opus 5.5, fresh

items.label: A
items.critique: Opens on the same 'Bah! X! Great big slimy ones' exclamation template and closes on 'Dead? All of 'em? Ha!', a formula shared with three other texts here. The exact gold figure and 'good gold in it for you' are tidy but stock.

items.label: B
items.critique: Plain, slightly clumsy exposition ('a foul little urchin has moved into the cave'), a key handed over mid-offer and a plot-gate reward (the petition) rather than gold. Odd but true Westwood mechanics.

items.label: C
items.critique: Same 'Bah! Scorpions!' / 'Dead? All of 'em? Ha!' frame as A; the causal backstory (Ogres took the place, vermin coming down) is neater world-building than Westwood bothered with, and 'That's fair, isn't it?' feels added for colour.

items.label: D
items.critique: Repeated 'mate', the bathing anecdote and 'a damn fine spell' have Westwood's offbeat humour; the long, literal journal line is typical of the original.

items.label: E
items.critique: The pet frog and the 'Loads and loads of money?' joke are classic Nox silliness, with the '?!' punctuation Westwood used freely.

items.label: F
items.critique: Exclamation opener, 'won't spare me a man' and 'Ha! My pigs can sleep easy' mirror J and the others too closely; every new text is built on the same beat sequence and grateful-but-poor sign-off.

items.label: G
items.critique: 'Ooooh, how can this be?' and the terse, slightly stilted plot handoff with no gold reward fit Westwood's story-quest lines.

items.label: H
items.critique: Same leech template as A in a different setting; the 'Ever since that Necromancer came' causal clause and 'You earned every piece of it!' recur across the new texts.

items.label: I
items.critique: Missing comma ('north of here and kidnapped'), 'my sweet sister' and the vague 'tokens of my appreciation' reward are Westwood's slightly rough register.

items.label: J
items.critique: Mirror of F (Bears, 'won't spare me a single man', Undead at the walls, 'just like I promised'), polished but formulaic.

tells: The new texts share one rigid template: an exclamation naming the pest ('Bah! Leeches!', 'Bears!'), a 'Great big ...' intensifier, a backstory clause tying the pest to the main villain, a promise of pay, then 'Dead? All of 'em? Ha!' / 'Ha! ...' and 'You earned every piece.' Repetition across texts gives them away more than any single line.
New texts pay an exact sum of gold (75, 80, 100); Westwood's rewards are often items, spells, keys or plot passes, or vague 'tokens of my appreciation'.
Westwood's lines carry odd jokes (pet frog, boots stolen while bathing, 'Loads and loads of money?'), small grammatical roughness and '?!' punctuation; the new ones are cleaner and more uniform.
New quest-givers explain why the trouble exists in world terms (since the Necromancer came, since the Ogres took the pass); Westwood rarely bothered.
